lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: # Deepening

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: How to deepen a cluster of shallow modules safely, given its dependencies. Assumes the vocabulary in [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) — **module**, **interface**, **seam**, **adapter**.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Dependency categories

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: When assessing a candidate for deepening, classify its dependencies. The category determines how the deepened module is tested across its seam.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ### 1. In-process

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Pure computation, in-memory state, no I/O. Always deepenable — merge the modules and test through the new interface directly. No adapter needed.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ### 2. Local-substitutable

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Dependencies that have local test stand-ins (PGLite for Postgres, in-memory filesystem). Deepenable if the stand-in exists. The deepened module is tested with the stand-in running in the test suite. The seam is internal; no port at the module's external interface.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ### 3. Remote but owned (Ports & Adapters)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Your own services across a network boundary (microservices, internal APIs). Define a **port** (interface) at the seam. The deep module owns the logic; the transport is injected as an **adapter**. Tests use an in-memory adapter. Production uses an HTTP/gRPC/queue adapter.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Recommendation shape: *"Define a port at the seam, implement an HTTP adapter for production and an in-memory adapter for testing, so the logic sits in one deep module even though it's deployed across a network."*

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ### 4. True external (Mock)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Third-party services (Stripe, Twilio, etc.) you don't control. The deepened module takes the external dependency as an injected port; tests provide a mock adapter.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Seam discipline

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - **One adapter means a hypothetical seam. Two adapters means a real one.** Don't introduce a port unless at least two adapters are justified (typically production + test). A single-adapter seam is just indirection.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - **Internal seams vs external seams.** A deep module can have internal seams (private to its implementation, used by its own tests) as well as the external seam at its interface. Don't expose internal seams through the interface just because tests use them.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Testing strategy: replace, don't layer

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Old unit tests on shallow modules become waste once tests at the deepened module's interface exist — delete them.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Write new tests at the deepened module's interface. The **interface is the test surface**.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Tests assert on observable outcomes through the interface, not internal state.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Tests should survive internal refactors — they describe behaviour, not implementation. If a test has to change when the implementation changes, it's testing past the interface.
